repositories.name: metadata-graph
repositories.reason: Owns the column model, ingestion consumer, metadata REST API and metadata.dataset.changed.v1 publisher, so it must suggest classifications from source tags, store steward overrides per column, expose a set/override endpoint and include classification in column responses and change events.

repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Spec of record for the metadata-graph OpenAPI and the event schemas, so the new classification endpoint, additive column fields, the additive event fields and the access-decision masking field must be defined here first.

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: REST clients must use its MetadataClient, so it needs classification fields on column models and a method to set/override a column classification, released as a backward-compatible minor version.

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: Produces ingestion.schema.discovered.v1, whose column entries currently carry only name/type/nullable, so it must additionally forward the source column comment and parsed tags (e.g. tags: pii,email) for classification suggestion.

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 and is the natural owner of access decisions, so it must store per-column classification from the event and return the columns to mask when the requester lacks a pii:read grant.

repositories.name: query-service
repositories.reason: Whichever service returns query results to data consumers (not present in the workspace) must apply the masked-column list from the access decision to result values.

repositories.name: data-quality-service
repositories.reason: Produces dq.result.published.v1 and runs DQ checks, so it must look up column classifications and apply PII-format validation rules to PII columns.

repositories.name: reporting-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1, which only gains additive optional fields, so its event parsing must be re-verified as a tolerant reader (unless it also serves query results to consumers, see open questions).

considered_not_impacted.name: graph database (GRAPH_DB_URL)
considered_not_impacted.reason: Infrastructure rather than a repository; the new column properties are additive node properties written by metadata-graph and need no separate repo change, though any schema/index migration would live in metadata-graph.

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].comment (raw source column comment) and columns[].tags (array of lower-case strings parsed from 'tags: pii,email'); absent means no tags.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional dataset.columns[].classification (PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII), columns[].classification_source (SUGGESTED|STEWARD) and columns[].tags; classification-only changes are published with the existing change_type COLUMNS_CHANGED so no new enum value is introduced.

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Each column object gains classification, classification_source, suggested_classification and tags fields; existing fields unchanged.

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column}/classification
contracts.description: Steward sets/overrides a column classification with body {classification, reason?}; validates the enum, returns the updated column (404 on unknown dataset/column, 400 INVALID_CLASSIFICATION), persists classification_source=STEWARD and publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1.

contracts.name: POST /v1/access-decisions
contracts.description: Access-decision response gains masked_columns (list of column names classified PII that must be masked because the requester lacks pii:read); path is inferred because the entitlements API is not in the workspace.

contracts.name: POST /v1/queries
contracts.description: Result values of masked columns are replaced by a mask token of unchanged column type/shape and the response gains optional masked_columns metadata; path is inferred because the query API is not in the workspace.

open_questions: Which repository returns query results to data consumers (query-service is inferred; is it reporting-service, a separate query gateway, or the warehouse layer)?
Exact names and APIs of the ingestion service, data-quality service and entitlements access-decision endpoint, none of which are in the workspace.
What classification do unclassified/existing columns get: none (null), INTERNAL by default, or a backfilled suggestion?
Should CONFIDENTIAL columns also be masked (and under which grant), or is masking strictly PII vs pii:read as the ticket states?
Who may call the classification override endpoint (steward role/grant name) and should overrides be audited and reversible to the suggested value?
What is the full tag-to-classification mapping (pii, email, phone, ssn, confidential, internal, public) and the precedence when tags conflict?
Should a steward override survive re-ingestion even if source tags later change, and should a tag change that raises sensitivity override a lower steward value?
Masking format: fixed token, null, partial (e.g. j***@x.com), or hash? Must masked values preserve type for typed consumers?
Which PII-format rules apply per PII subtype (email, phone, SSN) and where are rule definitions owned (data-quality-service config vs platform-contracts)?
Do strict-schema consumers of metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (entitlements-service, reporting-service) reject unknown fields, which would make the additive change effectively breaking?
Does platform-sdk generate its models from platform-contracts (implying a release ordering), and which versions follow platform-sdk 3.4.1 / platform-contracts 2.3.0?
